liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Friend Of The Devil, Little Red Rooster, and the second set are highlights [11]
- **Althea** (1 review): The soulful rendition of Althea is a highlight of the show [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **I Know You Rider**: with Mountain Jam tease [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-12-12.124542.aud.goldshine.sennheiser-mkh406-flyingm.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 170 min; rated 4.56/5 by 18 [1]
- **gd1980-12-12.175120.sbd.miller.remaster.31509.flac1644**: soundboard; 23 songs; 173 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1980-12-12.175907.nak700.ellner.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 173 min [4]
- **gd1980-12-12.fob.ellner.motb.89347.flac24**: source not stated; 22 songs; 167 min; rated 4.83/5 by 6 [6]. Said about its sound: Instruments and vocals are well-balanced, capturing the venue and present crowd nicely; Right channel gain was reduced by one to one and a half decibels; Small dropouts were repaired and clicks removed using Adobe Audition and other software [6][13]
- **gd1980-12-12.fob.glassberg.motb.89134.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 167 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [7]. Said about its sound: This recording is brighter, louder, and better than the other available audience version; The audience recording is highly listenable and crisp, though not technically perfect [8][9]

## Around the show

- Guests: Mountain Jam tease [1]
- This was the first show the band played after John Lennon was killed [12]
- The Swing Auditorium, an old airplane hangar, rocked and rolled solidly [14]
- An airplane later crashed into the venue, leaving only memories and tapes [14]
- The drive to San Bernardino was somber as John Lennon had been murdered four days earlier [1]
- The San Bernardino Swing Auditorium was described as a real sweatbox [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-12-12.124542.aud.goldshine.sennheiser-mkh406-flyingm.flac16**: taped by Ron Goldshine and John Musgrave with help from Mark the B-Man and Mike Martin (guarding the mic stands); transferred by Mike Martin; source: Source: 2 Sennheiser MKH 406 TUD microphones > Sony D5M (w/ Dolby B, Bias @ 70us on 3 TDK MA C-90 tapes); Copy of masters: Sony D5M (w/ Dolby, Bias @ 70us) >… [1]. Also: The uploader finally retired and had time to digitize their personal recordings [16]
- **gd1980-12-12.175120.sbd.miller.remaster.31509.flac1644**: transferred by Transfer and Remastering by Charlie Miller  November 14, 2025; source: SBD > Cassette (Nakamichi CR-7A) > DAT (Sony PCM-R500) [3]. Also: The uploader repaired vocal phase issues and repatched tape flips, pitch, and levels; Neil Sturtevant transferred the Mike Shoun tapes for this release [3]
- **gd1980-12-12.175907.nak700.ellner.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Ron Ellner; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Ron Ellner's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Nakamichi 550 (TDK MA C-90) through the tape flip in "Good Lovin'" Ron Ellner's Master (FOB)… [4]. Also: Bob Menke provided the master cassettes and first-generation reel recordings and transfers [4]
- **gd1980-12-12.fob.ellner.motb.89347.flac24**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert and SIRMick; source: 2 x Nakamichi CM-700 => Nakamichi 550 >> MAC [6]
- **gd1980-12-12.fob.glassberg.motb.89134.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ron Ellner; transferred by A. Egert and SIRMick; source: 2 x Nakamichi CM-700 => Nak550 >> MAC [7]
